content.title: Be on Your Own Side
content.scope: A Little More Room · Eight brief educational readings, with optional everyday practices. These are not diagnosis or treatment.

intent.subject: Be on Your Own Side
intent.direction: Explore a practical psychological perspective with ordinary examples and realistic limits.
intent.perspective: Public education; gentle, optional practices without clinical promises.

readings.label: A mistake is not your identity
readings.text: You can take responsibility for a mistake without turning yourself into the mistake. Self-compassion begins with that distinction: something went wrong, and you still deserve a useful, humane response.
readings.learn: You can take responsibility for a mistake without turning yourself into the mistake. Self-compassion begins with that distinction: something went wrong, and you still deserve a useful, humane response.

readings.label: Notice the tone
readings.text: Imagine forgetting an appointment. Your inner voice might say, I ruin everything. Pause long enough to hear the tone. Is it describing the problem, or attacking the whole person?
readings.learn: Imagine forgetting an appointment. Your inner voice might say, I ruin everything. Pause long enough to hear the tone. Is it describing the problem, or attacking the whole person?

readings.label: Describe what actually happened
readings.text: Try a more specific sentence: I missed an appointment, and someone was inconvenienced. Specific language leaves room for repair. A sweeping insult gives you much less information about what to do next.
readings.learn: Try a more specific sentence: I missed an appointment, and someone was inconvenienced. Specific language leaves room for repair. A sweeping insult gives you much less information about what to do next.

readings.label: Offer yourself a fair response
readings.text: Consider how you would speak to someone you respect. You might acknowledge the impact and help them work out a next step. That same combination of honesty and care can include you.
readings.learn: Consider how you would speak to someone you respect. You might acknowledge the impact and help them work out a next step. That same combination of honesty and care can include you.

readings.label: Neutral kindness is enough
readings.text: If warm words feel false, start with something neutral: this is difficult; what would help now? You do not have to manufacture affection or say an affirmation you cannot believe.
readings.learn: If warm words feel false, start with something neutral: this is difficult; what would help now? You do not have to manufacture affection or say an affirmation you cannot believe.

readings.label: Let kindness include repair
readings.text: Compassion does not erase responsibility. You can apologize, reschedule, or set a reminder. The question becomes, how can I respond constructively, rather than how harshly can I punish myself?
readings.learn: Compassion does not erase responsibility. You can apologize, reschedule, or set a reminder. The question becomes, how can I respond constructively, rather than how harshly can I punish myself?

readings.label: Choose one act of care
readings.text: A supportive action might be eating, resting, asking for assistance, or reducing an unrealistic demand. Choose something that fits your circumstances. Care does not have to be expensive or impressive.
readings.learn: A supportive action might be eating, resting, asking for assistance, or reducing an unrealistic demand. Choose something that fits your circumstances. Care does not have to be expensive or impressive.

readings.label: Do not grade your compassion
readings.text: If this feels awkward, that is not another failure. Try again gently, or seek support with a trusted professional. Self-compassion is a way of responding to difficulty, not a requirement to feel good.
